findings.title: Routine cleanup logs at Error level, generating false alerts
findings.body: The new code logs the cleanup batch with `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err)`. This is a normal/expected operational event during routine annotation cleanup, not an error. Logging it at Error level will fire false alerts on error-monitoring systems, pollute error pipelines, and dump the full list of IDs plus the constructed SQL condition into error logs every minute (after the cleanup.go ticker change). It also passes `"err", err` while `err` is always nil at that point (the function has already returned if it was non-nil). It should be `r.log.Info` or `r.log.Debug`, and the misleading `"err", err` key/value should be removed.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batch logged as Error
findings.body: `r.log.Error("cleaned annotations by time", "count", len(ids), "affected", x, "err", y)` is emitted on every successful cleanup batch. This logs a normal successful operation at Error level, producing repeated false-positive alerts whenever the cleanup runs. It also passes `"err", y` where `y` is always nil (since this log is reached only after a successful delete). It should be downgraded to `r.log.Info`/`Debug` and the spurious `"err"` field removed.

findings.title: MaxCount cleanup routine logged as Error
findings.body: `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by count", ...)` fires at Error level for routine MaxCount-based cleanup. Same problem as the MaxAge path: normal operations are reported as errors, and `"err", err` is always nil at that point. Should be `Info`/`Debug`.

findings.title: Successful MaxCount cleanup logged as Error
findings.body: `r.log.Error("cleaned annotations by count", ...)` is emitted on every successful MaxCount cleanup batch. Again, this is a normal success path, not an error. Downgrade to `Info`/`Debug` and remove the spurious `"err", y` field.

findings.title: Orphan-tag cleanup routine logged as Error
findings.body: `r.log.Error("Tags to clean", ...)` fires every time `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` is invoked by the cleanup ticker, even when there are zero orphans (`len(ids) == 0`). With the ticker now running every minute (see cleanup.go change), this floods error logs and triggers false alerts during normal operation. Should be `Info`/`Debug`.

findings.title: Successful orphan-tag cleanup logged as Error
findings.body: `r.log.Error("cleaned tags", ...)` is emitted on every successful orphan-tag cleanup batch. This is a normal success log, not an error. Downgrade to `Info`/`Debug` and drop the always-nil `"err", y` field.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker frequency bumped 10x without justification
findings.body: The PR is about fixing MySQL deadlocks in the annotation cleanup, but this change moves `ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`. That makes the entire cleanup routine (and the now-Err-logging annotation cleanup) run ten times as often. This is unrelated to the deadlock fix, multiplies database load unnecessarily, and combined with the Error-level logs above will multiply the false alerts accordingly. If a higher frequency is wanted, it should be a separate change with its own justification (e.g., a new config flag, defaulting to 10m).

findings.title: O(n²) string concatenation when building the SQLite inline IN-list
findings.body: When `r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit`, the code builds the IN-list with `values := fmt.Sprint(ids[0]); for _, v := range ids[1:] { values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) }`. Each `fmt.Sprintf` call copies the entire accumulator, so the total work is O(n²). With the newly added test case using a batch size of 32767, this is roughly a billion operations and ~hundreds of MB of garbage per cleanup batch, and it gets worse for any future larger batch sizes. Use `strings.Builder` (or `strings.Join`-style construction with a pre-sized buffer) so the build is O(n).

findings.title: Deadlock fix has no MySQL integration test coverage
findings.body: The new and renamed tests (`TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, `TestIntegrationOldAnnotationsAreDeletedFirst`) only exercise SQLite via `db.InitTestDB(t)`. The bug this PR fixes — annotations writes being rejected due to a deadlock with the cleanup job — is MySQL-specific (see referenced issue #64979). Without a MySQL integration test, a future regression in the locking pattern (e.g., re-introducing a subquery-based DELETE inside one transaction) would not be caught. The PR should include (or rely on an existing) MySQL integration test exercising concurrent inserts and the cleanup loop.

findings.title: Hard-coded SQLite parameter limit (999) ignores SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER in modern SQLite
findings.body: The condition `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` uses `const sqliteParameterLimit = 999`. SQLite >= 3.32.0 defaults SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER to 32766, and even older builds can be recompiled with higher limits. The new test case is even named "should not fail if batch size is larger than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER for SQLite >= 3.32.0", but the code itself still assumes 999, so for batch sizes between 1000 and 32766 the code unnecessarily takes the slow, O(n²), unsafe (no parameterization) inline path. The limit should be derived from a runtime check or configured, not hard-coded to 999.
